The story is tightly woven, with its beginning, middle, and end logically flowing into one another to explore the theme of holding onto the unexamined "leftovers" of past relationships. The mysterious elements introduced in the beginning—the dream of the flat, the blue linoleum, the kettle, and Rachel's seemingly useless comment about keys—are all given context and resolution by the end. Furthermore, the subplot involving Isabel's ex-partner, Gareth, and the old voicemail directly serves the main plot; it acts as the catalyst for Daniel to finally open up about his dreams and understand his own lingering attachments. Finally, the parallel imagery at the climax (Isabel steadying Daniel's knee in the canoe just as Rachel once had) brings the emotional arc to a satisfying and unified conclusion, allowing the haunting dream to finally subside.
